name: Doh Neiiong
subtitle: Khasi pork stewed in ground black sesame until the gravy turns dark and nutty

ingredients.qty: 700g belly and shoulder mixed, in 3cm cubes with the fat left on

ingredients.note: black sesame is what gives the gravy its colour; white seeds work but the dish stays grey-brown
barely any is needed — the pork renders plenty of its own fat

prepNotes: Ask for pork with a decent fat cap. Lean pork gives a thin, gritty gravy — the fat is what carries the sesame.
Grind the sesame with a little water into a paste, not a dry powder, and do it before you start cooking.
Bring the pork to room temperature so it browns instead of stewing when it hits the pan.

steps.text: Dry-roast the sesame seeds in a heavy pan over low heat for 4-5 minutes, shaking constantly, until they start to pop and smell strongly nutty.
steps.tip: Black seeds hide their colour, so go by smell and sound. Burnt sesame turns the whole dish bitter and there is no rescuing it.

steps.text: Cool the seeds completely, then blend with the chopped onion and 4 tbsp water to a thick, slightly coarse paste.
steps.tip: Cooling first matters — warm seeds go oily and smear instead of grinding.

steps.text: Put the pork in a pan with the turmeric, 1 tsp salt, the bay leaf and 300ml of the water. Bring to a boil and simmer covered 20 minutes, skimming the grey foam off the top.
Heat the oil in a kadhai and fry the sliced onion for 8 minutes until deep gold and shrunken.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook 2 minutes until the raw smell is gone.
Lift the pork out of its liquor into the kadhai, keeping the liquor. Add the cracked pepper and fry hard for 8 minutes, turning, until the cubes take on brown edges and the pan looks dry.
Stir in the sesame paste and cook 3 minutes, then add the reserved pork liquor and the remaining 200ml water.
steps.tip: Scrape the base as you add the liquid — everything stuck there is flavour.

steps.text: Simmer uncovered 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the gravy darkens, thickens enough to coat the pork, and fat beads at the rim.
steps.tip: Sesame catches on the base the moment you stop stirring. Keep the heat low.

steps.text: Add the green chillies, check the salt, and simmer 5 minutes more.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. The gravy sets solid when cold — reheat over low heat with 3-4 tbsp water, stirring, until it loosens. Freezes well for a month.
